extracted.intended_audience: general readers who want to be funnier (people practicing conversational humor, amateur comedians, aspiring performers)
extracted.subtask_description: Developing the mindset, material, and delivery skills to be funny in conversation, jokes, and live performance. Covers observing humor, crafting setups/punchlines, conversational riffing, ethical boundaries, and common delivery pitfalls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look at things from an absurd or unexpected angle
rubrics_metrics.description: Comedy lives in the gap between expectation and reality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek contrasts between what people expect and what actually happens; reframe ordinary situations to reveal the absurd.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep a humor journal
rubrics_metrics.description: Write down anything that makes you laugh and try to articulate WHY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect bits, observations, and triggers for laughs; analyze entries later to mine for material and patterns that work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be observant
rubrics_metrics.description: Funny people notice the small, weird, true details others ignore.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Train attention to specific, relatable details; those specifics often make jokes land because they feel true.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study comedians whose style resonates
rubrics_metrics.description: Read, watch, and study comedians; map what they do that lands with you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Break down timing, word choice, misdirection, and physicality in performances you admire to incorporate techniques into your own voice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Find what's already funny in the situation
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't try to be funny — try to find what's already funny in the situation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer discovery-based humor over forced jokes; look for inherent incongruities or shared experiences to highlight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Have a clear setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish the expected world in one sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a concise setup that orients the audience so the punch has a clear target to subvert; avoid overloading the setup with unnecessary detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Create misdirection in the setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Shape the setup so the punchline can pivot unexpectedly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lead the audience toward an obvious conclusion, then break that expectation with the punch; misdirection is the engine of many jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline goes at the end
rubrics_metrics.description: Punchline belongs at the end; never bury it mid-sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the payoff where the audience's attention is maximized; burying the punch reduces impact and causes missed laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the rule of three
rubrics_metrics.description: Pattern, pattern, break.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish a repetitive pattern twice then break it on the third item for comedic effect; the rule of three is a structural shortcut to surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time your pause
rubrics_metrics.description: A brief silence before the punch lets the audience lean in.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a pause (micro-silence) to build tension and give listeners a beat to anticipate the punchline; avoid overlong pauses that lose momentum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't laugh at your own joke before the punch lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid signaling the funniness before the audience has a chance to respond.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Let the audience react first; prematurely laughing at your own material can undercut their response and telegraph the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commit to the bit
rubrics_metrics.description: Half-hearted delivery kills the laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fully inhabit the character or premise of the joke; confident delivery — through voice, posture, and eye contact — sells the incongruity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Riff on what's already happening
rubrics_metrics.description: In-the-moment humor beats memorized jokes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use improvisational responses to current events in the conversation; callbacks and riffs tied to context feel fresher and more relatable than canned material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-deprecate sparingly
rubrics_metrics.description: A little self-deprecation is charming; a lot is sad.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use self-deprecation to lower threat and build rapport, but avoid undermining yourself excessively — it can become uncomfortable for audience and performer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the room
rubrics_metrics.description: Gauge tone, audience age, and comfort level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt material and delivery to the setting; risky or edgy jokes may be inappropriate depending on audience demographics and mood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid punching down
rubrics_metrics.description: Never target marginalized or vulnerable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim jokes at situations, yourself, or shared experiences rather than mocking people with less power; ethical targeting preserves respect and avoids harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: If a joke bombs, move on quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: Don't explain a failed joke; transition away.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acknowledging a failure briefly or changing topic preserves momentum; over-explaining the joke usually compounds the awkwardness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't repeat a joke that already landed once
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid repeating the same joke after it has already gotten a laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once the joke has landed, move forward — repeating reduces impact and can feel like trying to squeeze more out of a single payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't preface
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid setup lines like 'This is so funny, you'll die'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set expectations low and then exceed them; prefacing signals to the audience how to feel and can make the payoff fall flat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't be mean and call it a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: Cruelty isn't comedy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid masking nastiness as humor; mean-spirited remarks that harm others are poor comedic choices and frequently alienate audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don't force callbacks
rubrics_metrics.description: Let callbacks feel discovered rather than manufactured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use callbacks sparingly and organically; forced callbacks can feel contrived and reduce the naturalness of the set or conversation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup establishes a clear expectation (Is This Funny? rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: The setup should clearly define the expected scenario so subversion is meaningful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clear setup makes the punchline's contrast intelligible; fuzzy setups lead to confused or muted laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punchline subverts expectation in a connectable way (Is This Funny? rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: The punch should overturn the setup in a way the audience can relate to.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subversion must be intelligible and resonate with the audience's knowledge or experience to trigger laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word economy: every word earns its place (Is This Funny? rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use only necessary words; eliminate clutter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tighter language increases pace and comedic impact; extraneous words dilute the setup and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery includes a pause, eye contact, and commitment (Is This Funny? rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective delivery combines micro-timing, engagement, and conviction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pause for tension, make eye contact to connect, and commit physically/verbally to sell the joke.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target is appropriate (Is This Funny? rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer targets like self, situation, or shared experience — not vulnerable people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ethical targeting preserves audience goodwill; aim punches at safe, relatable subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: The audience laughs (the only real metric) (Is This Funny? rubric)
rubrics_metrics.description: Audience reaction—laughter—is the terminal criterion for success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use laugh response as the primary measure; if the audience doesn't laugh, reassess setup, punch, timing, or target.
